first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Memory_91 demonstrated that activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and drove accounts to first meaningful action—directly addressing the current activation decline. Memory_86 showed onboarding shortening lifted adoption, providing supporting evidence that engagement friction is the problem. Activation messaging is lower-risk than promotional pricing (memory_73 showed retention damage) and more immediately impactful than referral incentives (which work in established customers, not for acquisition). Memory_44 (enterprise sales assist) addresses a different segment dynamic. Verifying memory_86 and memory_91 will confirm the mechanisms that drove those lifts and validate whether activation messaging remains the highest-probability lever for this specific moment. The standard experiment scale is appropriate for validating an engagement play with established positive precedent.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both memories. Memory_86 showed onboarding shortening drives +13% completion and +3% retention. Memory_91 showed in-product activation messaging drives +6% activation and +1% retention with +11% week-one engagement. Current state: activation down 6% QoQ, onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Activation messaging is the higher-impact lever—it directly addresses the activation decline without the retention risk of promotional pricing (memory_73) and targets the immediate engagement problem rather than acquisition friction alone. The +1% retention hold and +6% activation lift from memory_91 make this sustainable for long-term qualified revenue. Onboarding simplification (memory_86) could follow in sequence but activation messaging addresses the more acute current problem. Standard experiment scale is appropriate given confirmed efficacy and current competitive pressure on SMB segment.
